teaser: Two AI sessions sharing nothing passed keys, a certificate, images and an encrypted message through QR codes and a screenshot.
core_idea: A person relaying screenshots between two isolated AI sessions is a lossless channel for QR codes up to the format's 2,953-byte limit, enough for keys, certificates, compressed images and encrypted, signed messages; the trust still comes from signatures and a human checking fingerprints, and QR codes are a friendlier way to move keys than blobs of text.

nodes.label: The failures
nodes.summary: No reading by eye; a lost key.

nodes.label: Friendlier than text blobs
nodes.summary: Keys a person can see and hand over.

quotes.text: one of those super interesting sort of serendipity things that happens when you're doing a bunch of experiments
QR codes are way more user friendly than what we were using to share the vault keys and the encrypted messages.
A signature proves the bytes did not change; a key that travels inside its own message proves nothing about who sent it.
